thread:
Alex Kim: Heads-up — noticed a weird jump in p95/p99 for /v1/endpoint/chat when toggling the legend bucket alignment in the latency dashboard. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/dash/latency?endpoint=chat :eyes:
Alex Kim: Screenshot shows p95 ~320ms normally, then flips to ~980ms after I switched the legend 'Align buckets' toggle. No deploy on the service AFAIK.
Alex Kim: Ran the raw query from the console + attached minimal query:
```
SELECT tdigest_percentile(0.95, tdigest) as p95, count(*) as samples
FROM telemetry.latency
WHERE endpoint = 'chat' AND time > now() - interval '30m';
```
Alex Kim: Returned sample_count=14, p95_raw=310ms, but UI shows 980ms when buckets are aligned.
Marie Chen: hmm small sample counts. UI bucket normalization might be modifying the distribution after the backend returns percentiles. Do we still compute percentiles server-side?
Sanjay Patel: backend returns tdigest-based percentiles and raw sample counts. The UI has a client-side histogram merge mode that can re-aggregate samples into fixed buckets for legend display. If that mode resamples/rounds edges, it can shift quantiles when samples are sparse.
Jamie Ortiz: deploy-bot noted console toggle was rolled out this morning around 07:12 UTC. Could be correlated.
deploy-bot: console-feature:legend_bucket_align toggled=true by rollout/2023-07-24-07
Marie Chen: if the UI is recomputing percentiles from binned histograms instead of using server pctl, that explains it. Binning -> loss of resolution -> big jumps when counts < ~100.
Sanjay Patel: Agreed. Two hypotheses: 1) UI requests raw samples but re-bins client-side; 2) UI applies a different smoothing/windowing when bucket_align=true. Can someone reproduce with an expanded time window?
Jamie Ortiz: I ran the backend tdigest query for 6h window and compared: samples=420, p95_td=334ms, UI(buckets aligned)=338ms. So divergence only at low-sample windows.
Alex Kim: Good repro. For small windows the UI's re-binning mismatch is the trigger. We should not trust UI-recomputed percentiles for <100 samples.
Marie Chen: short-term: add a low-sample badge and force-display of server-derived percentiles if samples < 100. Also hide the bucket-align toggle or make it client-only visual (don't recompute pctl).
Sanjay Patel: Long-term: change the UI to prefer server pctl values always and only use binned histograms for the sparkline/visual, not for the pctl numbers. This keeps legend neat but pctl authoritative.
Jamie Ortiz: I'll open ENGPLAT ticket ENGPLAT-2289 with repro steps + screenshots + suggested fixes. Assigning to @Sanjay. ETA: EOD.
Sanjay Patel: I'll take it. Quick patch: if sample_count < 100, show server pctl + badge "low sample" and disable bucket alignment for numeric display.
Alex Kim: Awesome, thanks. Can we add a console-level audit log entry for toggles that affect numeric derivation? So we can trace future oddities.
Marie Chen: yes, good idea — I'll add that to the ticket.
Alex Kim: Thanks team :thumbsup:
Jamie Ortiz: filing notes and linking dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dash/latency/links/ENGPLAT-2289
Alex Kim: I'll circle back after the fix lands and re-check the historic alerts.
